source.title: Perception, Action, and Intrinsic Motivation in Infants' Motor-Skill Development

confidence_rationale: Corbetta's account of infant reaching is the closest verifiable analogue to MECH-329's mechanism. She describes goal-directed reaching as originating, around 3-5 months, from a CASUAL CONTINGENT EVENT -- 'when the hand happens to contact a target' -- which 'provides new behavioral value', 'reinforces the motor action, and intrinsically motivates infants to attempt to reproduce the behavior.' This is structurally MECH-329's seeding story: an ACCIDENTAL contact, not a calibrated preference, is the originating event, and an intrinsic approach/motivation signal -- not a mature hedonic evaluation -- is what latches onto it and drives repetition. It places the seeding earlier than the 9-month third-person milestone in Behne 2005 and grounds the 'accidental benefit contact under approach drive' language directly. Confidence 0.58: it is a conceptual/review synthesis of the motor-development literature rather than a single decisive experiment, and 'intrinsic motivation' is not identical to mesolimbic incentive salience -- so it supports the accidental-contact-plus-approach-drive structure strongly while leaving the specific neuromodulatory identity open.
failure_signatures: Corbetta's 'intrinsic motivation' is a behavioural/motor-development construct, not specifically mesolimbic-dopamine incentive salience. Reading it as MECH-329's 'wanting' imports a neuromodulatory identification the paper does not make. If the infant motor-exploration drive is not dopaminergic incentive salience (cf. Opendak et al. 2025, who argue mesolimbic DA is not yet functional perinatally), MECH-329's specifically-mesolimbic framing is over-committed even though the accidental-contact-plus-approach-drive STRUCTURE survives.

The paper is a review/conceptual synthesis, not a controlled test of ordering. It does not directly measure that motivated reaching precedes calibrated preference; it asserts a developmental sequence consistent with that ordering. Treated as decisive evidence rather than as a well-grounded framework, it would overstate the case.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Infant goal-directed reaching emerges around 3-5 months from a casual contingent event -- the hand accidentally contacting a target -- which provides behavioural value, reinforces the action, and intrinsically motivates the infant to reproduce it; repeated perception-action cycles then refine the skill.
mapping.ree_translation: This is MECH-329's seeding mechanism in the human motor-development literature: an ACCIDENTAL benefit contact (hand-on-target), not a calibrated preference, is the originating event; an intrinsic approach/motivation signal latches onto it and drives repetition, structuring early goal-directed behaviour before any mature hedonic preference function is in place. It grounds the 'accidental benefit contacts under approach drive seed the first goals' clause directly and earlier than the 9-month attribution milestone.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Corbetta's 'intrinsic motivation' is not explicitly mesolimbic incentive salience; the entry supports the accidental-contact + approach-drive STRUCTURE of MECH-329, not the specific claim that the seeding signal is mesolimbic dopamine. Pair with Opendak et al. 2025 for the neuromodulatory-identity caveat.
mapping.source_context: Human infants, first year; review of perception-action and motor-skill (reaching) development.

confidence_components.notes: Good source quality (peer-reviewed review by a leading infant motor-development researcher in a respected venue). Mapping fidelity moderate-to-good: the accidental-contact-plus-intrinsic-motivation structure maps tightly, but the neuromodulatory identity (mesolimbic DA vs generic intrinsic motivation) is not pinned. Transfer risk moderate: review-level synthesis, not a single ordering experiment.
